To determine entanglement experimentally in polarization qubit pairs, we utilize quantum estimation theory to develop the most precise estimators possible, which we then apply to achieve optimal measurement accuracy. We conduct a series of experiments focused on measuring the amount of entanglement in various families of two-qubit two-photon states, using visibility measurements of quantum correlations to achieve the highest possible precision. Notably, using optimal estimators does not necessitate full state tomography; in fact, we compare the results to those obtained from tomographic reconstructions using two different sets of projectors, demonstrating the latter's reduced precision. Furthermore, we leverage optimal estimators to assess and compare the performance of different noise models describing decoherence effects that arise during entanglement generation.

The long-lived palm tree modes (PTM) found in the JET tokamak's edge plasma remain somewhat enigmatic despite detailed documentation. A recently investigated explanation suggests that these modes form when magnetic field lines become perturbed and travel along the edge field. However, a simpler alternative is presented here, which posits that these modes are actually localized structures within plasma turbulence that develop along the edge field. Evidence from JET and ASDEX Upgrade experiments indicates that these modes are closely related to benthic vortices - a type of plasma turbulence that carries current parallel to the magnetic field. A clear correlation exists between these benthic vortices and palm tree modes, and their collective behaviour closely resembles that of an individual perturbed field line peregrination mode. A statistical link between these structures and a lower edge plasma density concentration is found, which provides a possible physical basis for their emergence. A simplified model also shows how their rate of decay might be influenced by a type of edge plasma density control called the Edge Density Control System (EDCS). This research indicates that the underlying physics driving these experimentally observed modes is relatively simple and offers a more unified understanding of these perturbations in edge plasma.

Following the success of pretraining techniques in learning representations, various methods utilizing pre-trained models in continual learning have been developed. Some of these approaches build upon the pre-trained representations by implementing mechanisms for continual learning with minimal or no updates to the backbone models. In this study, we challenge the necessity of complex models by comparing a simpler alternative - leveraging the stability provided by pre-trained models without further modifications. We evaluate this strategy using state-of-the-art architectures and benchmarks for lifelong learning, finding that it consistently delivers reliable results. We demonstrate that a pre-trained "frozen" model can replicate the performance of existing continual learning methods such as REPLAY, REGROWTH, and PODNet while avoiding the associated losses. The study's findings are presented in detail on the standard CIFAR10 and CIFAR100 datasets.

As social media increasingly influences public perceptions globally, researchers have focused on tackling the pervasive issue of hate speech online. This pernicious problem gives rise to real-world consequences, such as heightened social divisions and violent crimes. Previous studies have employed automated hate speech detection methods, but they often fall short by overlooking broader social and contextual nuances. Furthermore, few attempts have been made to explore the explainability of such models, given the severe social and legal repercussions of inaccurate predictions. Our research introduces a sophisticated, deep learning-based framework that integrates multimodal inputs. This innovative network leverages its capacity to learn from diverse, mixed data to identify hate speech patterns. By incorporating a multi-layered attention mechanism, our model is able to prioritize hate-related indicators, thereby yielding superior results. Our experiments, conducted across three datasets from various domains - news articles, social media posts, and online forums - demonstrate that our approach surpasses existing state-of-the-art hate speech detection techniques in accuracy. Moreover, our analysis of the underlying mechanism reveals that our model's hate-indicative findings are remarkably consistent across datasets. This sheds light on the universal hate speech patterns, which can be utilized for informed hate detection across various settings.

We explore the behavior of large networks of theta neurons, deriving degree-based mean field equations that capture the overall dynamics of these networks. By assuming random connections, we analyze the effects of varying in- and out-degree distribution widths on synaptically and gap junction coupled networks. Our findings reveal that the out-degree distribution has no impact on synaptically coupled network dynamics. Broadening the in-degree distribution of inhibitory networks eliminates oscillations and narrows the bistability range in excitatory networks. Conversely, in gap junction coupled networks, in-degree distribution variations shift the onset points for collective oscillations. Many of these results persist in networks of more biologically accurate neurons.

Recent years have seen increasing interest in Automatic Program Repair (APR) from both industry and academic sectors. As part of an effort to leverage recent advancements in deep learning, we propose the use of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) to generate and explore modified versions of programs and their potential application in the APR process. In our initial examination, we focused on the simplicity of semantic patch testing, where repair templates are known in advance, and we aimed to generate and evaluate modified versions of the input program source code that precisely correspond to the repair templates as exemplified by existing studies. Although our simulation-based results indicate that it's feasible to generate code closely aligned with the repair templates via GANs, the performance falls short of the efficacy observed in related works applying APR techniques directly. In the long run, we anticipate that APR can be revitalized through the integration of deep learning techniques, and our work, though still in its early stages, represents an exploratory step in this direction.

This study introduces a general framework for the capacity region of a complex interference channel with interconnected user pairs, characterized by a collection of interconnected rectangles, with each rectangle defined by paired rates of mutual information. While this formula cannot be directly computed due to its interdependence, with one value dependent on the others, it provides a valuable mathematical structure, with each intersection point representing the optimal rate distribution for a specific channel arrangement. To tackle this challenge, we developed an algorithm for computing the lower mutual information rate boundary for pairs of interconnected users, with each user connected to two others. Additionally, we established a key relationship between this rate and the overall interference channel capacity in the asymptotic, high signal-to-noise ratio range. Furthermore, a numerical implementation of these concepts was achieved using a collection of surface fitting methods. To verify the efficiency of this approach, we performed a comparative analysis with existing literature on interference channel capacity for interconnected user pairs.

We aim to broaden the established flow analysis technique, which typically operates within the $p_x$-$p_y$ plane, by introducing flow coefficients based on the angular distributions within the $p_x$-$p_z$ and $p_y$-$p_z$ planes. Introducing new flow coefficients, denoted $u_n$ and $w_n$, in conjunction with $v_n$, reveals these coefficients are highly responsive to a nuclear substance's equation-of-state. Utilizing $u_n$ and $w_n$, in conjunction with $v_n$, enables the thorough assessment of an equation-of-state beyond what $v_n$ can facilitate, making this novel analysis more informative. For example, our study applies the Ultra-relativistic Quantum Molecular Dynamics model to simulate $130$Sn$+$197Au collisions at 1 GeV, demonstrating how the energy dependence of $u_n$ and $w_n$ differs substantially from $v_n$, thereby allowing for nuanced discernment of various equation-of-state models.

The timely detection of COVID-19 remains a significant research priority, offering potential advantages in the initial assessment and management of suspected patients, while also reducing hospitalizations and mitigating pressure on healthcare systems. Consequently, a comprehensive study examining the use of machine learning techniques for COVID-19 detection in patients with mild symptoms has been undertaken. This study employed a large combined dataset from two influential competitions (Flow-based Multipath CNN-LSTM and MULPAR), utilizing eight sophisticated machine learning methods to train and assess models. Crucially, the research design focuses on detecting mild COVID-19 cases using clinical data, thereby facilitating early identification and separation from non-infected patients. Moreover, a analysis of statistical scores revealed that machine learning methods outperformed simpler statistical models, while a hyperparameter optimization experiment using two influential algorithms further refined the performance of machine learning techniques. Notably, the research highlights the benefits of incorporating multipath convolutional networks in model architecture design.

A Graph Neural Network (GNN) is an effective neural network architecture that processes graph data through message passing. Due to its excellent performance in node classification, link prediction, and ranking, it has been applied to a variety of wireless communication systems. However, compared to its potential, there is still a significant gap in current research. This survey first provides an introduction to GNN, followed by a detailed discussion of the challenges posed by wireless communication systems. Next, it presents a comprehensive overview of the latest GNN techniques used in these systems. Finally, it identifies future areas for research and development in this field.

The threat of homicide death tolls has raised concerns worldwide about crime safety, prompting governments to seek effective solutions to prevent violent deaths. For instance, Brazil is experiencing a similar issue with its high homicide rate, making it necessary to understand the underlying factors driving this trend. By using a widespread multi-agent simulation model known as the Social Influence Model, this study aimed to replicate the observed increase in homicide rates across different regions of Brazil. According to our simulation results using data for 26 Brazilian states, we found that the Social Influence Model was able to replicate the national decline in homicide rates as well as the varying patterns of homicide rates in individual states. Additionally, our analysis highlighted important differences in demographic homicide rates, with higher rates among young people and males. While our model was unable to exactly match the magnitude of homicide rates in each state, we believe that the Social Influence Model holds promise for use in predictive modeling and spatial analysis of homicide rates.

Our goal is to modify stochastic gradient descent (SGD) to be adaptive to (i) 
variance $\sigma^2$ in stochastic gradients and (ii) problem-dependent parameters.
When optimizing smooth, strongly-convex functions with condition number $\kappa$, we 
prove that $T$ iterations of SGD with step sizes that decrease exponentially and 
knowledge of $\sigma^2$ enable convergence to the optimal solution within error of 
$\sigma^2 / \kappa^2 + \frac{1}{T}$. For a variety of problem settings, we show that 
SGD converges at a rate of $O(1 / \kappa^2)$ without knowing $\sigma^2$. Our 
findings also enable the application of SGD to non-convex optimization, where we 
demonstrate that $T$ iterations of SGD with step sizes that decrease exponentially 
enable a rate-optimality bound of $\epsilon$ with $O(\frac{\sigma^2 T_0 \log (T_0 T)}{\kappa^2})$ 
where $T_0$ is a known parameter. Our work specifically utilizes finding new bounds 
for the vector power mean. Our technique builds upon a recent paper of Z. Lim, and we 
generalize it to smooth, strongly-convex and non-convex optimization problems. Our 
approach also utilizes a variation of Z. Lim's technique which was discovered during 
a discussion

Axions emerge as a logical outcome of the Peccei-Quinn mechanism, the leading explanation for the strong-CP issue.  Variants of axions known as axion-like particles (ALPs) also arise in our understanding of the fundamental forces.  Although axions and ALPs with conventional properties are challenging to detect directly, ALPs can be identified through their influence on photon properties.  This identification method involves a specific technique called polarimetry that uses measurements of polarized components to detect ALPs by differentiating between polarized and unpolarized states of radiations.  By demonstrating the potential of polarimetry to detect ALPs, we have performed the first simulation of an experiment looking for ALPs through changes in photon polarization, showing that this method could be a viable ALP detection method in various situations.

The occupation number over time is examined for a bosonic oscillator coupled to heat baths with fermionic and bosonic components.  Given that genuine memory storage necessitates deviations from equilibrium, this problem's solution – yielding occupation numbers for both systems – sheds light on this requirement.  Moreover, the dynamical behavior of this oscillator in non-equilibrium steady states is also considered.

Developing robots with skilled hands that can effectively grasp and manipulate objects is an essential yet complex challenge. In comparison to other object-grasping fields, dexterous grasping has been understudied, mainly due to a shortage in high-quality training datasets and associated models. To address this issue, we present DexGraspNet - a comprehensive dataset and deep learning-based method for robotic dexterous grasping. The dataset, which comprises a massive 125,921 semantic grasp semantic grasp configurations, is one of the largest of its kind and offers a high level of diversity in viewed orientations and environments. Utilizing the dataset, we achieve significant performance advancements in a grasping network evaluation, showcasing an accuracy increase of 10% and 5% in depth-complete and half-view settings, respectively. The project's source code is publicly available at https://github.com/GT-STAR-Lab/DexGraspNet.

A novel approach is proposed to create and assess a respiratory motion-compensated four-dimensional T2-weighted MRI sequence, which is essential in radiology and radiotherapy treatments guided by MRI. A variable-time data collection technique is initially used to acquire a rough respiratory motion scan, followed by a customized gating period during which MRI signals with low phase variability are collected and high phase variability is restricted. A golden-segment phase encoding correction protocol is developed to correct respiratory motion, which involves assessing respiratory phases from a rough scan, calculating correction vectors, and applying them to the phase encoding dimension. This technique is evaluated through simulations, models, and actual experiments, comparing golden-segment correction with NEX (number of echoes per respiratory cycle) methods. Experiments demonstrate that in cases of periodic motion, golden-segment correction outperforms NEX approaches, specifically reducing bias and maintaining variability reduction. However, in cases with random motion, it's suggested that using probabilistic models could further enhance the technique's performance. Four-dimensional MRI sequences using this golden-segment correction protocol are proposed for T2-weighted imaging, enabling high-quality, motion-stable, 4D MRI images.

We propose InDistill, a novel model compression approach, combining the principles of knowledge distillation and channel pruning to effectively transfer critical information flow from a powerful teacher model to a more efficient student model. Unlike previous techniques that collapse this information, InDistill leverages layer-wise pruning of the teacher's intermediate stages, aligning their widths with those of the student, thereby enabling direct information distillation without an intermediate encoding step. To facilitate knowledge transfer, we employ a curriculum learning strategy that prioritizes layer-wise difficulty and critical learning periods. Through these advancements, InDistill significantly outperforms current state-of-the-art methods, achieving enhanced results on a range of benchmarks, including ImageNet and CIFAR-100.

Two submersion functions from the set of two-dimensional real numbers to the set of real numbers are defined, and their respective level set foliations are examined. The equivalence of these functions topologically implies the topological equivalence of their foliations. Conversely, this relationship is not always valid; however, we define a specific class of linear-like functions with sufficient complexity and provide criteria under which the converse is true, establishing a definitive topological invariant for this particular subset of linear-like functions.

Ecosystems that naturally thrive in dry environments have become increasingly vulnerable due to the rising threats of degradation and declining productivity. One notable aspect of these ecosystems is the spontaneous formation of plant patterns that can visually appeal and help regulate their response to stress. Research has shown that herbivory is a critical mechanism behind the creation of these patterns and the functioning of the entire ecosystem. Despite a theoretical understanding of this process, the application of these principles to real-world ecosystems is hindered by the complex interactions within them. We investigated how vegetation arrangement affects grazing pressure in real-world ecosystems through a study of a sheep grazing area in southern France. The results of this study show that areas with higher vegetation, lower density, and isolated patterns experience higher grazing pressure. This is consistent with theoretical predictions and suggests that patterns of plant distribution may impact the overall health and resilience of ecosystems subjected to selective stress.

A well-known dimensionality reduction technique called CountSketch employs randomized linear measurements to offer estimations of $x^TSx$ and $\|x\|^2$ with minimal bias and bounded variance. This document presents a novel CountSketch extension that enables the computation of any quadratic polynomial $f(x^Tx)$ with precise estimates while ensuring large-bad outcomes remain rare through the application of tail inequalities.

A python-based program, ipie, has been developed for auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo simulations, along with its implementation on central and graphical processing units and interfacing with PySCF. Preliminary timing benchmarks compared ipie with Quantum/fortran-based Quantum Monte Carlo programs, showing ipie performs similarly in parallel computations. Additionally, timings for calculating the energy of water and alanine dipeptide molecules at various auxiliary-field scaling factors indicated ipie's graphical processing unit implementation outperforms the central processing unit version. Integration with PySCF enables easy use of ipie with the Electronic Structure Library, including parallel and graphical processing unit calculations for molecular, cluster, and plane-wave systems.

High-frequency trading could greatly benefit from first-generation quasi-quantum communication technologies. This text examines a game theory scenario in which three players make decisions, using last knowledge of past outcomes, and defines a strategy that achieves optimal results from a quantum perspective. Due to the trading interval being extremely brief, quantum effects can be considered over extremely brief periods. This allows for the integration of quantum principles into trading strategies and the concept of quantum communication to improve transaction timing, providing a possible application for quasi-quantum capabilities. Such an application could serve as a type of algorithmic HFT, which could be executed by a quasi-quantum system demonstrating capabilities like superposition, entanglement, or non-locality. Additionally, this trade scheme could also benefit from quantum key distribution and quasi-quantum capabilities such as entanglement swapping and non-local storage.

We examine a mechanism design problem for selling $k$ items to unit-demand buyers with private valuations for each item between zero and one, where the distribution of individual valuations follows a uniform $[0,1]$ distribution for each item. Since $k$ is unknown to the seller, we use a generalized second-price allocation method and prove a ${\epsilon}$-Nash equilibrium exists, and our work demonstrates that our model has a comparable computational complexity of $O(k^{{\epsilon}}\log k)$. Additionally, we investigate an online variant of this problem where after each $t$ rounds of purchase, the buyer's valuation for each item is drawn independently from a uniform distribution. In this variant, our work designs an $O(\sqrt{\ln t}/\sqrt{k})$ revenue guarantee for the buyer, and this result is optimistic since it shows that the buyer's revenue can increase linearly with $\ln t$, and our work is the first to provide a lower bound for seller revenue by showing that for sufficiently large $k$, the buyer's revenue is at least $k/2^{O(\ln t/\log k)}$.

To facilitate abstractive summarization, we've introduced an efficient planning mechanism that enables the generation of grounded summaries. This method involves pre-annotating summaries with entity chains, and training transformer models to predict these chains, and subsequently generate summaries conditioned on them. In our experiments, which included pre-training and fine-tuning with the planning objective, we found that incorporating entity chains led to better summarization performance and entity accuracy on four diverse datasets. Notably, this method outperformed previous state-of-the-art methods in terms of Rouge metrics for the XSum and SAMSum datasets. Furthermore, our findings indicate that incorporating entity chains allows for more effective hallucination control, and we were able to improve faithfulness of generated summaries by prompting the model to omit irrelevant information.

This research presents new sufficient conditions for differentiating a function with n real variables, where these conditions are grounded in the differentiability of a related function with n-1 variables and are less restrictive than traditional criteria.

Human vocal synchronization in social interactions provides valuable information about a person's cognitive behaviors, suggesting the importance of understanding entrainment patterns in conversations. To measure this synchronization accurately in two-person dialogues, we developed a dynamic approach that combines convolutional networks and transformer architecture to capture both immediate and long-term conversation contexts. By incorporating attention layers for analyzing both internal and external interactions, our model can learn meaningful patterns in social encounters across various domains. Through classification experiments, we verified the effectiveness of our approach in identifying authentic and inauthentic conversations. Moreover, when testing our model with individuals having Autism Spectrum Disorder, our results indicate a strong statistical link between our entrainment measure and relevant clinical symptoms, including hyper-systemizing.

A recent study applied a realizability technique to establish the meaning of a quantum lambda calculus, which lacks a clear subject reduction strategy, within a pre-Topological Model. This led to a comprehensive framework outlining the acceptable data types in such a quantum setting. This contribution begins by explaining the key principles behind the pre-Topological Model and then demonstrates how this model can be used to prove the correctness of a quantum lambda calculus with data types, all without relying on a subject reduction strategy. Building upon this, we develop a typing discipline that enforces a form of static type checking for such quantum calculi, which rely on a pre-Topological Model with both additive and multiplicative connectives. It's worth noting that while such models can be used for both, the primary focus here is on the additive connection. Finally, we explore an untyped pre-Topological Model, which serves as a foundation for a future quantum lambda calculus without data types.

Analytical calculations have been performed for two types of quasiparticle excitation energies per particle in systems of up to seven electrons within both the Laughlin theory and composite fermions theory, accounting for the comprehensive jellium potential consisting of electron-electron, electron-background, and background-background interactions. The findings support that the composite fermions wavefunction outperforms the Laughlin wavefunction in energy for two quasiparticle configurations, albeit the difference in their energies diminishes with growing system size.

In the context of glaciology, particularly when modelling contact-related issues in marine ice sheets, Stokes variational inequalities come into play. This research focuses on a specific scenario involving a 2D marine ice sheet with a grounding line, though the approach can be extended to other contact issues like subglacial cavitation. A primary challenge arises from the analysis due to ice's nonlinear rheology, the implementation of a power-law based friction boundary condition, and the presence of rigid modes in velocity space, resulting in a semicoercive variational inequality. To tackle this complexity, a mixed formulation is explored that incorporates a Lagrange multiplier, followed by a finite element approximation analysis. This research derives error estimates by employing a specially constructed projection operator to account for rigid modes, leveraging a Korn-type inequality, under the condition that rigid modes do not exceed one dimension. To corroborate these findings, numerical results are provided.

Using observations from KCWI and NOEMA, we studied a distant starburst galaxy, examining how star formation-driven gas outflows are linked to other properties of the galaxy. Our data show a nearly linear relationship between outflow mass and star formation rates, as well as a significant correlation between outflow mass and gas usage times. In systems with high star formation rates, the outflow mass is greater than the mass of newly formed stars, indicating an inefficient use of gas. We also found that, in these areas, the outflow mass is greater than the mass of newly formed stars, the outflow speed approaches the speed of sound, and there is a large amount of ionized gas visible. Our findings are consistent with a model of a dense, turbulent region where stars and outflows are continuously created and interact.

Our research examined the connection between initial anisotropic geometry and anisotropic flow within a multiphase transport model, specifically for 200 GeV Au+Au and Cu+Cu collisions. Contrary to elliptical flow's dependence on centrality, we discovered minimal variation in triangular flow centrality. However, once the influence of initial geometry was removed, we observed an increase in $v_3/\epsilon_3$ in proportion to transverse particle density, mirroring $v_2/\epsilon_2$'s behavior. Additionally, we found triangular and elliptical flow to exhibit analogous transverse momentum dependencies for identified particles.

Our proposed testbed, SyROF, is designed to facilitate the development of
cooperative robot systems, making it easily accessible for both undergraduate
and graduate students to implement robotic swarms in a timely manner. To achieve
this goal, we developed SyROF, an innovative testbed that features a user-friendly,
high-level programming environment supporting the Timed Input Estimation
Algorithm. This advanced algorithm enables efficient synchronization of multiple
robots moving objects, including a transparent, distributed control mechanism.
We incorporated the VREP simulator into SyROF, equipping it with the necessary tools
to accelerate the design and evaluation of robotic swarm systems. Furthermore,
we incorporated a user-friendly, high-level programming environment called PySyROF
into SyROF, allowing users to program robotic swarm behaviors using intuitive
commands. We have now incorporated PySyROF into both a simulated environment
within VREP and a real-world testbed featuring four TX2 robots, making it
accessible via a GitHub repository under an open-source framework.

Deep neural network training for semantic segmentation requires considerable effort,
so many researchers opt for pre-training their model on a different task before
further refining it using a annotated dataset of a segmentation task. It has
previously been found that using depth estimation for pre-training is more
beneficial than using colour and no additional benefits are gained by using
three-stream networks that incorporate colour and depth information. Rather than
using labelled data for pre-training, an unsupervised approach can be taken,
leveraging the depth estimation capability of modern networks without requiring
any depth maps. It is shown that using this unlabeled data for pre-training, using
only depth estimates, outperforms a pre-training method that uses colour and
achieves comparable results to other pre-training methods that use three-stream
networks that incorporate colour and depth information. Additionally, it is found
that using two labelled datasets of different domains for fine-tuning and
transferring knowledge to a target task is more beneficial than using a single
dataset.

Let's consider the set of all analytic functions defined within the unit disk in the complex plane and have their absolute value strictly less than one, denoted by the symbol. The classical Bohr's inequality deals with a power series that converges in the same unit disk, and we can derive that its terms satisfy the inequality for a certain fixed constant where. The function representing this fixed constant is known as the Bohr radius, and further research aimed to find the maximum possible value of this constant for given polynomials of a certain degree. The paper primarily focuses on finding new estimates for polynomials of a certain degree in the context of Bohr's inequality for analytic functions with positive real coefficients and then extends these findings to a more general form of polynomials in the same context.

A nonparametric measure of correlation known as Kendall's tau is examined, along with an efficient method for estimating its value from data. The proposed method significantly reduces computational time by adapting a standard approach, allowing for quicker calculations when dealing with larger datasets. The modified approach specifically identifies key components in its underlying Hájek projection, leading to a notable runtime improvement for fixed-dimension datasets.

The number of connected devices has seen tremendous growth, creating vast volumes of diverse data that intertwine with our physical world. The Edge Intelligence System has emerged to harness edge computing and AI, facilitating intelligent services through powerful processing and near-instant decision-making. With a central server orchestrating entire systems, existing frameworks still struggle with security risks, but they offer a crucial stepping stone for future applications, like real-time traffic management, which, together with suitable techniques, can ensure reliable service provision. This paper outlines a framework for traffic management on highways, combining an operator's centralized capabilities with decentralized edge computing capabilities to provide robust services. We present an end-to-end system for highway traffic management, discussing its implementation and a related field experiment. The results show that this system's integrity remains unimpacted even when attacked, securely operating within a malicious environment. Moreover, the edge-based edge intelligence component's functionality can still be maintained should the central server fall victim to malicious activity. This groundbreaking setup has implications for other service providers, enabling them to ensure the reliability and resilience of their intelligent services.

This study focuses on the application of the Euler characteristic for advanced topological data analysis in multi-variable spaces. Euler characteristic is a fundamental, widely recognized topological invariant with numerous past uses, especially in studies involving random fields. Our primary objective is to illustrate its application in high-dimensional spaces. While employing more powerful invariants like homology remains an active area of research, the theoretical and computational feasibility of the Euler characteristic make it an attractive intermediate step for multi-variable topological analysis. We demonstrate its practicality by using artificial datasets and a real-world example involving diabetic retinopathy detection from retinal images.

Our analysis focuses on an adjusted predator-prey model based on Holling-Tanner's equations with a Type II predation response, also taking into account a strong Allee effect affecting prey population growth. We build on previous studies by Saez and Gonzalez-Olivares and Arancibia-Ibarra and Gonzalez-Olivares who studied similar Holling-Tanner models with a mild Allee effect. In this modified model, complex dynamics are exhibited, including separations in the phase space, separate existence regions for coexistence and extinction scenarios. Moreover, a boundary between stable and unstable system behavior is established, ultimately manifesting an inverse Allee effect in one system parameter's influence.

The Hirsch Conjecture was a theory claiming that a d-dimensional polytope with n faces cannot exceed a diameter of n - d. This assumption was contested by Santos, whose findings led to the conclusion that some linear programming methods cannot perform optimally within n - d iterations. This series of research was initiated by a novel algorithm, the facet pivot method, proposed in the first paper. This second paper verifies the efficacy of the facet pivot method, confirming it can solve linear programming problems in at most n - d iterations, motivated by Smale's mathematical problem 9, first introduced in the late 90s.

We explore in an associative ring R with identity, the scarcity of k-torsion in the NK1GQ(R), which are Bass nil-groups for general and unitary quadratic groups. Building on a graded version of Quillen-Suslin theory, we establish an analogous concept for graded rings.

This paper undertakes a thorough comparison of the comprehensive, off-shell computation for pp -> ttj events, particularly focusing on the dileptonic decay channel, with an approximation based on the narrow width assumption. Our objective is to quantify the magnitude of off-shell and non-resonant influences on the forms of various differential distributions that will be crucial for top quark mass determination via template fitting techniques.

The susceptibility of facial recognition systems to fraudulent presentations restricts their adoption in high-stakes applications. Effective countermeasures against these deceptive attempts are vital for the safe integration of facial recognition technology. Current approaches have shown limitations, often failing to account for the full scope of attacks while being overly complex and optimized solely for specific forms of deception. In this context, we introduce Attenzione-Net, a general-purpose system capable of detecting all forms of live and spoofing attacks through the analysis of both authentic and deceptive facial images. Our innovative solution can adapt to various attack types and settings without exhaustive retraining, distinguishing it from existing methods. Our research encompasses a comprehensive evaluation across multiple datasets, presenting an substantial comparison of licensed and unlicensed methods. Our findings reveal that, in real-world scenarios, where users may not consistently present high-quality images, the differences in performance between licensed and unlicensed methods are negligible. Moreover, Attenzione-Net demonstrates the ability to correctly reject over 99.9% of all known types of spoofing attacks without the need for extensive retraining.

Deep reinforcement learning stands out as a promising AI paradigm for guiding decision-making without explicit guidance, making it an ideal choice for self-driving applications with unpredictable scenarios. Despite the potential, its widespread adoption is hindered by significant hurdles, notably its slow rate of learning from trial and error. In particular, tasks requiring high precision such as autonomous driving pose a challenge due to the sheer volume of finely nuanced data involved, rendering supervised learning approaches impractical. In order to efficiently leverage the benefits of both domains, we introduce a new value decomposition technique called "World-Data-Action" that enables efficient data application. We further enhance our framework by introducing a new agent architecture. In a comprehensive evaluation, our approach has been shown to achieve improved performance on a high-level driving reward, ultimately paving the way for seamless transition to a low-level reward in a semi-supervised setting, surpassing current benchmarks in self-supervised learning.

Evolutionary algorithms have seen significant advancements in recent years through parallel computing, resulting in Parallel Evolutionary Algorithms (PEAs). However, a major limitation in Asynchronous PEAs (APEAs) arises from idling computing nodes after each run. A significant problem arises when APEAs favor search areas evaluated quicker, thereby skewing the search distribution towards better areas discovered early. This paper aims to investigate this bias, assess its impact on APEAs, and provide insights for mitigating its effects. We examine APEAs in relation to diverse tasks, including multi-modal, high-dimensional problems and synthetic tests. The results indicate a substantial skew in the population towards earlier evaluated solutions. Notably, the multi-modal nature of HSBA and NSGA-III shows varying extents of bias. A possible remedy for reducing the bias is implementing a more equitable distribution of evaluations across the population. The paper concludes with a comprehensive understanding of bias in Asynchronous PEAs and a potential remedy to reduce its impact.

The recent microlensing event OGLE-2017-BLG-1434 involved a cold super-Earth planet located among a group of stars that are thought to be young and all share a similar kinematic feature. This planet, with a mass roughly a tenth of a Jupiter mass, serves as an ideal testing ground for a theory proposing that stars and their associated planets possess nearly unique mass ratios. According to this concept, which was already put to the test by several earlier events, we analyzed the mass ratio between the host star and its planet following the event OGLE-2017-BLG-1434. We gathered data from the survey as well as from the track the event, which together provide a detailed photometric coverage. This coverage allowed us to pinpoint the distance to the system, the angle of the light source relative to the observer, and the impact of the moving crowd, which helped us verify the mass of the host star. Interestingly, the mass ratio in this OGLE-2017-BLG-1434 event turned out to be quite close to a pivot point of an empirical relationship that describes how a planet's mass correlates with its host star's mass - a relationship that was derived from eight other microlensing events involving eight different stars. Taking into consideration the likelihood of a system containing a cold super-Earth, we found the probability of the mass of the host star being greater than a certain value to be around 70%.
